findings.claim: The plan names a risk it does not settle and leaves it out of `Could invalidate this plan`: 2.3.2 onward builds with Go 1.27.3, whose crypto/x509 rejects some intermediate chains, and the plan says only a live call to Ollama Cloud, Gemini and typesafe shows whether it bites. If it bites on any upstream, 2.6.0 is the wrong target (the same reasoning risk 2 uses), and the plan finds out only after the apply has run 12 one-way store migrations, so the way back is a dump restore plus a re-pin. This can be checked before the apply without touching the store: run the local maximhq/bifrost:v2.6.0 image (already pulled) with the bifrost.hcl provider blocks and real or bogus keys, and call one model on each of ollama, gemini and typesafe. A 401/403 or 200 from the upstream means TLS passed; an x509 or certificate error means it did not. Spike question: does Bifrost 2.6.0 complete a TLS handshake with each configured upstream (ollama.com, Gemini, typesafe's default base URL) as 2.3.1 does? Settle it by spike or list it as an operator-accepted risk.

O1 `needs` leaves out O3. Moving `bifrost_version` to 2.6.0 in services.tf fails `test_bifrost_is_pinned_to_2_3_1` (cli/tests/test_bifrost_version.py asserts pins == ['2.3.1']), and moving the test alone fails it the other way. Neither can ship without the other, so O1 and O3's test half cannot be split as the facts allow. Either O1 needs O3, or the pin test belongs in O1's touches and O3 keeps only the component page.

O2 `fixes: P1`, but taking a dump does not fix 'Bifrost runs 2.3.1'. The problem O2 answers (the 2.3.1 to 2.6.0 store migrations are one-way, so a failed upgrade has no way back without a dump) is in the prose and in G2 but is not listed under Problems. Add that problem and point O2 at it.
The Go 1.27.3 x509 risk is now risk 2 and settled by spike:bifrost-update-2-6/3, which reached all three upstreams through TLS on 2.6.0 and 2.3.1 with a working negative control.
O1 now needs O2 and O3.
P3 names the one-way migrations and O2 fixes P3.

Eval row r2 is unmet and can no longer be met: no dump of the bifrost store was taken before the apply, and the apply has already run the one-way 2.3.1 to 2.6.0 migrations. The skip rests on an operator instruction relayed by the implementer. The plan (step 3, O2, G2) and row r2 were never amended, so the signed contract still requires the dump. Only the operator can accept the loss of the rollback and amend or waive r2. Another implementer round cannot fix this.

The new version-history paragraph says Go 1.27.3's x509 checks accept the chains of ollama.com, Gemini and typesafe, citing spike /3. That spike ran from the devcontainer, not the cluster nodes, and the only live upstream call after the apply went to Gemini. The page drops that caveat. The paragraph also uses two semicolon splices, which the docs slop rule flags.
The TLS risk is still listed and is re-settled for 2.7.0 by spike:bifrost-update-2-6/6, which got upstream HTTP errors from all three hosts on 2.7.0 and 2.6.0 and a working untrusted-root control.
O1 needs O3, so the pin and the pin test move together.
P3 names the one-way migrations and O2 fixes P3.

The plan says 2.6.0 to 2.7.0 "adds two migrations, both reversible" that "add MCP client columns" (Intent step 3 and the 2.7.0 paragraph), and eval row r2 requires the component page to say so. The transports/v2.7.0 release notes list eight migrations, two of them non-reversible: `widen_batch_jobs_provider_status_and_endpoint` and `relay_logs_add_job_debug_widen_job_status` (the latter also carries an upstream warning about locks on `relay_logs`). Spike 5 shows `add_key_service_tier_column`, a non-MCP migration, running on 2.7.0. So the record O2 and r2 ask for would be false, and P3/O2 are incomplete: once 2.7.0 applies there is no way back to 2.6.0 either, not only to 2.3.1. Fix the migration facts in the prose, P3, O2 and r2 (no restore point to 2.3.1 or to 2.6.0).

The plan treats skipping the dump as costless because "a dump taken now holds 2.6.0's schema" and 2.7.0's migrations are reversible. With two one-way 2.7.0 migrations, a dump taken now is the only restore point to the 2.6.0 that is live and working, so the reason the plan gives for skipping it no longer holds. The operator's "Forget the backup. Just do it." was given about the earlier dump; the plan should record that the operator waives a dump knowing 2.6.0 to 2.7.0 is also one-way, or take a dump of the 2.6.0 store before the apply. The scope (dump or no dump) is the operator's call, not the plan's.
